subject: Dedicated capacity GPU family request and temporary hold
messages:
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@curahealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@curahealth.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU family requirement and reservation hold

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we like the runtime characteristics and the cost forecast looks promising. We have an upcoming pilot (Q2) that requires a guaranteed H100-class family for inference (model family requires model-level kernels and full FP16 performance). A few asks from procurement/infra that we need confirmed before issuing a PO: 

- Ability to reserve 48 dedicated GPUs (H100-class) for a 12 month initial commitment.
- Temporary reservation hold: we ask Redwood to place a 30–90 day hold on the reservation without billing while our PO and internal approvals clear.
- Burst capacity: permission to spike to 120 GPUs for short windows (we expect up to 72 hours once per month during the pilot).
- Overage concession: reduced overage rate for first 60 days (we'd like a 20% discount off published overage for that window).

Procurement indicated they can sign within 30 days of a mutually agreeable SOW and DocuSign, but legal needs the hold and overage terms in writing. I attached a draft SOW and a hardware matrix so you can see the workload profile.

Can you confirm whether this is possible and what approvals you need internally? Happy to set a call if helpful.

Best,
Dana
Dana Liu
Head of ML Infrastructure
CuraHealth
Attachments: cura_sow_draft_v2.pdf, hw_matrix.xlsx
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@curahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU family requirement and reservation hold

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear ask and the files.

Short answer: we can scope this, but the reservation-hold + H100-specific guarantee + deep overage concession are nonstandard and require deal desk + exec signoff. I will escalate immediately.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll pull in Deal Desk and Finance for a term proposal (aiming for a 48 GPU reserved block, documented burst windows, and a temporary hold duration).
- If we can get an executive signoff on a limited hold and overage concession, I’ll deliver an updated SOW and DocuSign link by end of day Thursday.
- If that timeline doesn't work for you, suggest a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow morning.

Appreciate the flexibility — I’ll follow up after internal alignment.

Thanks,

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Jan 2028 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: CuraHealth ask — executive approval request (H100 reservation hold + overage concession)

Team — forwarding CuraHealth's note (below). High-level commercials and recommendation: 

Summary of ask:
- Reserve 48 H100-class GPUs for Dedicated (12mo initial term).
- Temporary reservation hold (customer requests 30–90 days without billing while PO clears).
- Burst: allow spikes to 120 GPUs for up to 72 hours (expected once per month during pilot).
- Overage: 20% off published overage rate for first 60 days.

Customer background: CuraHealth is a mid-market healthcare SaaS with a $1.2M ARR pilot potential and strong strategic fit for our healthcare reference case. They move fast but procurement needs an explicit hold before issuing a PO. They've committed to a 12-month term once internal signoffs are cleared.

Commercial/legal considerations and risk: 
- Pricing risk on the H100 family and displacement on short notice.
- Reservation hold without billing is precedent-setting — risk of unused capacity if PO stalls beyond requested window.
- Burst to 120 GPUs creates demand spikes that may affect regional capacity planning.

Suggested approval (practical compromise):
- Approve a 90-day hold (max) on the reservation; billing paused for the hold period but customer must deliver a PO within 30 days or provide cadence updates; hold expires at 90 days.
- Approve burst up to 100 GPUs (cap) for spike windows, limited to 48-hour contiguous windows, max 4 windows in the 90-day pilot period.
- Approve a 15% overage concession for the first 60 days (instead of requested 20%).
- Require a one-time implementation fee of $25,000 to offset operational priority and capacity gating.
- Legal to add explicit SLA and fallback policies; DocuSign required before provisioning beyond a 10-day provisional hold.

Recommendation: seek Laura or Lauren exec signoff on the above modified terms to move to DocuSign.

Attachments: cura_sow_draft_v2.pdf, hw_matrix.xlsx, deal_summary.pdf

Thanks — Alex
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Jan 2028 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: CuraHealth ask — executive approval request (H100 reservation hold + overage concession)

Alex — reviewed. I authorize a narrower set of concessions than requested, with the conditions below. Please ensure Legal and Finance are looped immediately and prepare the updated SOW/DocuSign.

Approved terms (executive signoff):
- Reservation hold: up to 90 days maximum, billing paused during hold. Customer must provide PO within 30 days; otherwise we require written cadence updates every 14 days.
- Burst: cap burst to 100 GPUs (not 120) and limit each contiguous burst to 48 hours. Allow a maximum of 4 burst windows in the 90-day period.
- Overage concession: 15% discount off published overage rates for the first 60 days after billing starts.
- One-time implementation fee: $25,000 billed on first invoice.
- Provisioning guardrails: provision only after DocuSign is executed for the agreed SOW; we can offer a provisional 10-day hold while DocuSign is routed for signatures.

Conditions: legal to add explicit capacity rollback and fallback to compatible model families if H100 capacity is constrained; Finance to confirm accounting treatment for the hold. If CuraHealth insists on a 120 GPU burst or longer hold we decline — escalate back.

Signed — Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
